q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a knapsack sprayer?
title: Knapsack sprayer carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the plastic tank, pump parts, lance, hose and straps per sprayer and multiply by supplier figures, adding the battery and motor for battery sprayers. Add moulding and assembly energy, then divide the plant's energy by sprayers made.

ul: Pump parts, brass or plastic nozzle and lance.
Hose, straps and, for battery models, a battery and motor.
Blow moulding or rotomoulding the tank.

p: Report per sprayer by type and tank capacity. A battery sprayer carries a battery footprint a manual one does not.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 28,400 / 20,000 = 1.420 kg CO2 per unit
Add plastics, pump parts and any battery for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
